fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, acting under the People's Bank of China (PBOC); complementary authority for the Taiwanese investor side is the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) together with the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Chinese renminbi is convertible for current-account items (trade in goods/services, dividends, royalties) under a documentary compliance and genuine-transaction review. Capital-account items (foreign direct investment, offshore lending, reinvestment of undistributed profits, equity disposal) require SAFE registration and case-by-case approval. Profit repatriation from the WFOE to the Taiwanese parent encounters the following hurdles: (i) completion of annual corporate income tax audit and CIT filing; (ii) confirmation that distributable profits are calculated from lawfully audited financial statements; (iii) application of withholding tax at 10% (domestic statutory rate) or a reduced rate under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement, typically 10% for dividends; (iv) submission of the dividend resolution, tax clearance, and a bank payment application to the custodian bank, which then updates the FDI registration and executes the remittance. The entire process is bank-mediated and subject to beneficial-owner scrutiny and anti-treaty-shopping rules. On the Taiwan side, the parent must receive and clear the remittance through its designated foreign-currency account; Taiwan imposes no inward conversion restriction for mainland dividends, though capital-gains rules may differ.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China no longer imposes mandatory conversion ratios for current-account foreign-exchange receipts. Export proceeds (goods and services) must be repatriated to the WFOE's onshore foreign-currency account through a designated bank within the statutory period, generally within 180 days of the export declaration or service-invoice date for A-class enterprises, or as otherwise determined under the SAFE trade-forex monitoring system. All receipts must be credited to the entity's trade-forex income account, matched against underlying customs declaration or service contract, and reported in the SAFE international income/expenditure transaction database. The WFOE may retain the foreign currency on the account or convert it to RMB at market rates. For service exports exceeding the threshold, a tax certificate (Cross-Border Service Trade Payment) may be required.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore fintech EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut, Airwallex) are not licensed to open domestic RMB or foreign-currency settlement accounts in China and cannot submit SAFE filings on behalf of the onshore entity. They may be used passively as an offshore collection conduit for foreign customers, with onward remittance to the WFOE's domestic account via a partner licensed bank; however, all capital injections and profit remittances must go through the regulated banking channel. Any EMI arrangement must not obscure the underlying cross-border transaction, or it will trigger anti-money-laundering scrutiny.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal representative (or a director whose identity is on the corporate registration) must generally attend the initial account-opening interview at the bank branch, either physically or via an approved video conference. For foreign legal-person shareholders, a notarized and legalized board resolution appointing the local operator is accepted; however, physical presence of the appointed operator at the bank is still required in most state-chartered banks. Fully remote opening is only available for private individuals under the central-bank e-banking scheme, not for corporate WFOEs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder is an offshore legal entity with no visible economic nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of deposit of registered capital, office lease, payroll records, corporate bank statements, tax returns in the shareholder jurisdiction, and a shareholder reference from a bank in good standing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Health-EMR SaaS business may implicate personal health data transfers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cybersecurity Classified Protection (MLPS 2.0) compliance report, PIPL data-impact assessment, information security management system certification (ISO/IEC 27001), and a privacy policy confirming no unlawful cross-border transfer of patient data.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multiple shell layers or mixed beneficial-ownership jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transparent chain-of-title register through ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declarations, CRS/FATCA self-certification, notarized copies of organizational documents, and a written source-of-wealth statement for each UBO.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwanese shareholder must remit registered capital from its own account in Taiwan (or an offshore account) using SWIFT MT103. The remittance must include the wire reference 'FDI investment in WFOE registered capital' and the Chinese bank's capital-account transaction code (e.g., 6220). Prior to receipt, the WFOE must complete the Foreign-Exchange Business Registration (FDI) with SAFE through the custodian bank, obtaining the FDI registration certificate. On receipt, the bank will credit the foreign-currency capital account and offer RMB conversion at settlement rate; a second conversion (from CNY to TWD) is not done onshore. The capital must not be used for any RMB loan collateral or investment outside the approved business scope.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service exports (EMR SaaS subscriptions, implementation fees, maintenance), the principal rail is SWIFT MT103 for payment orders in USD, CNY, or EUR. Each outward remittance above $50,000 (or CNY equivalent) requires a tax voucher from the local tax authority (service-trade/foreign-exchange payment certificate), the service contract, invoice, and proof of service delivery. Commercial letters of credit are possible for large project-based engagements, but the standard workflow is open-account with upfront or milestone invoices. Chinese banks will process the credit only after verifying the real trade nature and completing the tax declaration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward contracts (CNY/USD, CNY/TWD via bank) contracted by the WFOE onshore, underlying genuine trade exposures, with no speculative margin trading.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term USD/CNY funding swaps, subject to SAFE registration and bank credit approval.
FX options on a non-margin basis (risk-reversal, knock-in/knock-out) for hedging specific transaction exposure.
CNH deliverable forwards or NDFs on the offshore market for the Taiwanese parent to hedge the conversion risk of its CNY-denominated investment returns; not directly booked by the onshore WFOE.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report on Business Information (企业年度报告公示)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fixed calendar window: 1 January – 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to publish by the deadline results in inclusion in the Abnormal Operation List; if not rectified within 3 years, registration may be revoked after public announcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Information Report (外商投资年度信息报告)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and SAMR Joint Annual Reporting Platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fixed calendar window: 1 January – 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing may incur an administrative fine of RMB 10,000–50,000 and inclusion in credit supervision records; rectification order may be issued.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Settlement Return and audited financial statements (企业所得税年度汇算清缴及审计报告)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local competent tax authority under the State Taxation Administration (STA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fixed calendar window: 1 January – 31 May of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of RMB 2,000–10,000; late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax; risk of tax audit and inclusion in tax credit blacklist.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No turnover or asset exemption: every WFOE limited-liability entity must obtain an annual independent audit of its financial statements by a licensed PRC CPA firm as part of the annual settlement filing package.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/China GAAP), substantially converged with IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foreign Investment Annual Information Report requires annual confirmation of all shareholders and actual controllers; any shareholding transfer in the preceding year must be reflected in that report. The SAMR/MOFCOM joint database is the authoritative UBO confirmation record; there is no separate public annual UBO declaration.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200–USD 3,500 per annum for a registered office or agency address arrangement in a Tier-1 Chinese city; physical premises lease excluded.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–USD 8,000 per annum for the compulsory CPA audit of a HealthTech SaaS WFOE.
